purpose: Versioned country-to-field registry for the World Relational Atlas. It separates Tim/Potatoverse axis assignments from empirical institutions while preserving overlap, uncertainty and provenance.
boundary: North, West, East and South are project interpretive fields, not borders, sovereignty, citizenship, ethnicity, consent or legal alignment. Countries may overlap fields. Empirical memberships such as BRICS, EU, NATO, ASEAN and Pacific institutions remain separate evidence layers.

brics.label: BRICS
brics.meaning: empirical BRICS backbone; visually coupled to East but not identical to it

evidence_model.explicit: Directly recovered Tim country-list or field statement.
evidence_model.recovered: Repeated or structurally consistent project formulation recovered from conversation/archive material.
evidence_model.corroborated: Project assignment that also maps onto a strong observable relationship such as EU, NATO, ASEAN, Pacific regional architecture or BRICS, without treating that institution as the cause of the assignment.
evidence_model.provisional: Current analytical hypothesis or newly suggested assignment not yet backed by a recovered project statement.
evidence_model.unknown: Insufficient project evidence; do not color by inference alone.

north.notes: Recovered core runs Canada/Greenland through the North Atlantic, Scandinavia and continental Europe toward Ukraine and Türkiye. The field is empirically reinforced by dense NATO/EU/North-Atlantic relationships but is not identical to either institution: Canada is NATO but not EU; Ireland is EU but not NATO; Türkiye is NATO but not EU; Greenland/Faroe constitutional geography differs from EU membership; Ukraine is an EU candidate with accession negotiations underway rather than an EU member.
north.confidence: high for named 2026 arc; mixed at UK, Russia and Mesopotamian edges

west.status: developed but broader and less institutionally bounded than North
west.notes: Recovered West is U.S.-centered and Atlantic/American. South America was described as West-primary unless specifically pulled toward East/North. Observable institutions show why this cannot be a simple alliance map: MERCOSUR joins Brazil and Bolivia to Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay across the project West/East hinge; AUKUS and Five-Eyes-type security ties strongly connect Australia, the UK, Canada and New Zealand to the Western security sphere while those countries may also occupy North or South project fields.
west.confidence: high at USA/Israel; medium across wider Americas and Indo-Pacific overlaps

east.status: developed relational field; explicitly not synonymous with BRICS
east.notes: Recovered East is Eurasian/Asian plus selected BRICS-linked nodes. Official BRICS material describes BRICS as a Global South political-diplomatic coordination forum, not an Eastern alliance. Its membership spans South America, Eurasia, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia. ASEAN likewise spans project East and South assignments, reinforcing a bridge/gradient model in Southeast Asia rather than a hard East/South border.
east.confidence: high at China/Russia/India and recovered Asian assignments; medium where BRICS is only corroborating context

south.notes: Recovered material points toward an Australia/New Zealand/Pacific and Indian-Ocean/southern-African maritime field. Official Pacific regional architecture strongly supports treating New Zealand, Australia and Papua New Guinea as a coherent Pacific relationship cluster, but this is corroboration rather than proof of Timic South assignment. African Union geography separately identifies Southern Africa as a real geographic region; AU membership itself must never be converted into project South because the AU covers the entire continent. Papua New Guinea remains provisional until a direct Tim assignment is recovered.
south.confidence: medium at Australia/New Zealand and southern-maritime logic; provisional for Papua New Guinea and wider African expansion

BRICS.interpretive_use: Corroborating relational context for East and South-South connectivity only; never an automatic East assignment.

NATO.interpretive_use: Explains part of the dense North/West security graph, but does not define either project field.

EU.interpretive_use: Strong institutional backbone inside the European portion of North, while North also includes non-EU nodes and candidates.

ASEAN.interpretive_use: Observable Southeast Asian regional layer crossing project East/South boundaries; Timor-Leste joined on 26 October 2025.

African_Union_regions.interpretive_use: Use AU five-region geography to distinguish real North/East/Central/West/Southern African geography from project fields. Do not equate Africa with South.

Pacific.interpretive_use: Pacific regional architecture corroborates an Australia/New Zealand/Pacific relationship field. Papua New Guinea and New Zealand are both Pacific Islands Forum members, but that fact does not itself settle project South status.

MERCOSUR.interpretive_use: Demonstrates that observable South American integration cuts across the project West/East hinge; use as an overlap edge, not a quadrant rule.

bridge_zones.note: Bridge zones are analytically more informative than forcing mutually exclusive quadrants. They describe overlapping relationships, not territorial boundaries.

classification_rule: Prefer recovered explicit Tim assignments; preserve overlaps; attach confidence/provenance; mark inferred or developing assignments as provisional; use real-world institutions only as corroborating relationship layers, never as automatic project-field assignments.
